title: ProjectConfig
description:
Project-tier configuration parsed from `ocx.toml`.

A flat `[tools]` table is the implicit default group; `[group.<name>]`
tables add optional named groups. Values are registry-qualified package
references, `registry/repo[:tag][@digest]`; a bare tag with no registry
(`cmake = "3.28"`) is rejected. A bare repository with no tag and no digest
(`cmake = "ocx.sh/cmake"`) parses as `:latest`; a digest-pinned entry gets
no default tag, since the digest is the canonical pin. Unknown keys are a
parse error.

tools.description:
Tools in the reserved `default` group (the top-level `[tools]` table in
`ocx.toml`). Values are fully-qualified package references.

env.description:
Environment variables for the default group; `[env]` in TOML.

Stands to `[group.<name>.env]` as `[tools]` does to
`[group.<name>.tools]`. It does not change which packages resolve, so an
edit never forces a re-lock.

group.description:
Named additive groups; `[group.<name>]` in TOML. `default` is reserved:
a literal `[group.default]` declaration is a parse error.

package.description:
Per-package resolve-time settings; `[package."<id>"]` in TOML, keyed by
the canonical author string `registry/repo[:tag]`.

Resolve-time policy, not a tool binding: a `no-patches` edit never
invalidates `ocx.lock`.

lazy-mode.description:
Toolchain-tier `lazy-mode`, the least specific config tier: outranked by
`[group.<g>]`, `[package."<id>"]` and the CLI flag. Absent falls through
to `OCX_LAZY_MODE`; it does not mean `never`. An edit never invalidates
`ocx.lock`.

lazy-report.description:
Toolchain-tier `lazy-report`. Absent falls through to `OCX_LAZY_REPORT`,
then to `silent`. An edit never invalidates `ocx.lock`.

activate.description:
Toolchain-tier `activate` mode: how a project's rendered toolchain
reaches a shell — per-prompt environment composition (`env`, the
default), a `PATH` entry for `<home>/toolchain/active/bin` (`bin`), or
neither (`none`). Absent falls through to `OCX_TOOLCHAIN_ACTIVATE`, then
to `env`. An unrecognized value is a parse error (exit 78). An edit
never invalidates `ocx.lock`.

pinned.description:
Toolchain-tier `pinned`: whether composed paths follow the rendered
`links/<group>/<entry>` links (`false`, the default) or pin to digest
roots (`true`). Absent falls through to `OCX_TOOLCHAIN_PINNED`. An edit
never invalidates `ocx.lock`.

trust.description:
Identity-pinned verification policies; `[[trust.policy]]` in TOML.

Consumed by `ocx package verify`, where it pools (array-append) with the
`config.toml` tiers. Resolve-time policy, not a tool binding: a policy
edit never invalidates `ocx.lock`.

ProjectEnv.description: Environment variables applied to binaries run from this project. Keys matching OCX_* or __OCX_* are rejected: a checked-in file must not be able to reconfigure how ocx itself resolves. Values are literal — no interpolation.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for a constant: replaces any existing value of the variable.

type.description: `constant` replaces the variable's value; `path` prepends to it; `list` appends to it.

separator.description: For `list` only: the string this contribution is joined to the variable's existing value with. Omit it to inherit whatever separator another contributor to the same key declared, or a single space if none did.

value.description: The literal value. For `path`, a relative value resolves against the project root; an absolute one passes through.

ModifierKind.description: How a declared value combines with the variable's existing value.

Group.description:
A named group's body: `[group.<name>.tools]` and `[group.<name>.env]`.

Exactly two optional sub-tables, nothing else: a tool binding written
directly under `[group.<name>]` is a parse error. A tool may still be named
`env` or `tools`; it is just a key inside `tools`.

tools.description:
Tool bindings for this group. Values are fully-qualified package
references, validated exactly as `[tools]` is.

env.description: Environment variables applied when this group is selected.

lazy-mode.description:
Group-tier `lazy-mode` override: outranks the toolchain tier and is
outranked by `[package."<id>"]` and the CLI flag. Absent inherits from
the toolchain tier; it does not mean `never`. An edit never invalidates
`ocx.lock`.

LazyMode.description:
Whether a declared tool composes onto `PATH` eagerly or as a shim that
defers content materialization to first invocation.

Wire values are `"never"` and `"always"`; any other value is a parse error,
never a silent default.

oneOf.description:
Compose eagerly: content materializes before the tool reaches `PATH`.
The default when every tier of the resolution ladder is absent.

Compose a shim: content materializes on the first invocation of one
of the tool's declared names.

PackageSettings.description:
Per-package resolve-time settings: `[package."<registry/repo[:tag]>"]`.

`no-patches = true` declines the site-tier companion overlay for that base,
except that a system-required patch still applies (enforcement beats
opt-out). The opt-out is version-independent: it keys on canonical
`registry/repository` and applies to every installed version. Unknown keys
are a parse error.

no-patches.description:
Decline the site-tier companion overlay for this base.

A system-required patch still applies (enforcement beats opt-out).

lazy-mode.description:
Package-tier `lazy-mode` override, the most specific config tier: only
the CLI flag outranks it. Absent inherits from the group and toolchain
tiers; it does not mean `never`. An edit never invalidates `ocx.lock`.

lazy-report.description:
Package-tier `lazy-report` override. Absent inherits from the toolchain
tier. An edit never invalidates `ocx.lock`.

LazyReport.description:
Whether a shim's first-invocation materialization renders progress.

Under `progress`, failing to open the controlling terminal (`/dev/tty`,
`CONOUT$`) degrades to `silent`, never to an error. Errors still go to
stderr regardless of this setting.

oneOf.description: No progress channel is opened for a first-invocation materialization.
Render progress for a first-invocation materialization, best-effort.

ActivateMode.description:
How a rendered toolchain home reaches a shell's environment.

Wire values are `"env"`, `"bin"` and `"none"`; any other `ocx.toml` value
is a parse error (exit 78), never a silent default.

oneOf.description: Compose the toolchain environment on every prompt. The default.

Put `<home>/toolchain/active/bin` on `PATH` and compose nothing else, so a
tool is resolved by its launcher trampoline at invocation time.
Neither. The reconciler withdraws whatever it owns and adds nothing.

TrustConfig.description: Container for the `[trust]` config section (`[[trust.policy]]` entries).

policy.description: The declared policies. Empty when `[trust]` is present but lists none.

sigstore.description:
Sigstore trust material for a self-hosted stack (`[trust.sigstore]`).

Read from the operator `config.toml` tiers only. The project `ocx.toml`
also accepts a `[trust]` table, but its `sigstore` sub-table is never
consulted.

TrustPolicy.description:
A single `[[trust.policy]]` entry.

One `signers` array names everyone this policy accepts, each entry tagged
`kind = "keyless"` or `kind = "key"`. Acceptance is ANY-of, so **adding a
signer always widens what verifies, never narrows it**.

```toml
[[trust.policy]]
scope = "ghcr.io/acme/*"
# or, to carve a subtree back out:
# scope = { include = ["ghcr.io/acme/*"], exclude = ["ghcr.io/acme/experimental/*"] }

signers = [
  { kind = "keyless",
    identity = "https://github.com/acme/tool/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v1.2.3",
    oidc_issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" },
]
```

A policy left with no usable signer (an absent or empty `signers`, only unknown `kind`s, or a
misspelled field that parses as an unknown key) is refused and fails closed, never widening.

scope.description:
Which packages this policy applies to: one prefix pattern, or an include/exclude set of them.

A pattern with no `*` matches the target's canonical `registry/repository` on `/`-separated
path-segment boundaries: `ghcr.io/acme/tool` matches that exact repo and any sub-path under it
(`ghcr.io/acme/tool/plugin`), but **not** a sibling that merely shares the prefix text, such as
`ghcr.io/acme/tool-cli`. A trailing `/*` covers the subtree; a mid-string `*` is a literal-prefix
substring glob.

```toml
scope = "ghcr.io/acme/*"
scope = { include = ["ghcr.io/acme/*"], exclude = ["ghcr.io/acme/experimental/*"] }
```

Absent reads exactly like `""`: a catch-all, as is an empty `include` with no `exclude`.

builder.description:
Expected SLSA provenance builder identity, matched against the
provenance predicate during attestation verify.

Ignored in signature mode, without an error.

signers.description:
The signers this policy accepts: an **ANY-of** set, each entry tagged
`kind = "keyless"` or `kind = "key"`.

```toml
signers = [
  { kind = "keyless", identity = "release@acme.example", oidc_issuer = "https://accounts.google.com" },
  { kind = "key",     key = "etc/acme-release.pub" },
]
```

**Every entry added here widens what verifies**: a new signer is a new way to pass, never a new
condition to satisfy. Absent reads as empty, and an empty set is a **configuration error**, not a
catch-all. A mis-spelled entry leaves no signer behind and fails closed the same way.

oneOf.description: One scope pattern. Segment-bounded without a `*`, literal-prefix glob with one; the empty string is a catch-all.
Patterns to cover, minus patterns to carve back out. A target matches when it matches at least one `include` (an empty `include` is a catch-all) and no `exclude`.

include.description: Patterns the policy covers. Empty is a catch-all.

exclude.description: Patterns carved back out. Beats `include` wherever both match.

SignerSpec.description:
One entry of a policy's `signers = [...]` array, tagged on `kind` with the
signer's fields flat beside the tag:

```toml
[[trust.policy]]
scope = "ghcr.io/acme/*"
signers = [
  { kind = "keyless", identity = "release@acme.example", oidc_issuer = "https://accounts.google.com" },
  { kind = "key", key = "etc/acme-release.pub" },
]
```

An empty array is a configuration error, never a catch-all.

oneOf.description:
A `kind` this build does not know — an entry written by a newer ocx.

It narrows: it accepts nobody, and a sibling `keyless` entry in the same
policy keeps working. A policy whose signers are *all* unknown is refused
with an error naming it.

KeylessMatcher.description:
A `kind = "keyless"` signer: which Sigstore identity may sign.

Exactly one of `identity` / `identity_regexp` must be set — both or neither
is a configuration error — and `oidc_issuer` must be present.

identity.description:
Exact expected certificate SAN (byte-equal).

Mutually exclusive with `identity_regexp`.

identity_regexp.description:
Regex the certificate SAN must match in full (anchored `\A…\z`).

Mutually exclusive with `identity`.

KeyMatcher.description:
The `kind = "key"` signer: one public key, by reference or inline.

Exactly one of `key` / `key_pem` must be set. There is no `key_regexp`: a
public key is a fixed value, not a pattern.

`ocx config push` inlines the reference form into `key_pem` at publish time.

key.description:
A key reference (`[scheme://]<rest>`), the same spelling `--key` takes on the command line.

Mutually exclusive with `key_pem`. Unrestricted in a local tier (project, operator or user
config on the author's own disk), where a relative reference resolves against the directory of
the config file that declared it. Refused in a managed-config payload: publishing fails with an
error naming `key_pem` as the fix, and a payload an older ocx published anyway has this field
dropped at load time rather than read.

key_pem.description:
Verbatim SPKI PEM.

Mutually exclusive with `key`.

SigstoreTrust.description:
The `[trust.sigstore]` sub-table: where verification gets its trust root
when the stack is self-hosted rather than the Sigstore public good.

Every field is optional and the whole sub-table may be absent — omitting it
reproduces the public-good behaviour exactly.

trusted_root.description:
Path to a Sigstore trusted-root JSON, or a directory holding
`trusted_root.json`.

A relative path resolves against the directory of the `config.toml`
that declared it — rewritten to absolute at load time, so the same
value means the same file regardless of the process working directory.
Mutually exclusive with `trusted_root_json`.

trusted_root_json.description:
The trusted-root document inlined verbatim.

This is the form a fleet receives: `ocx config push` reads a path-form
`trusted_root` at publish time and inlines it here. Mutually exclusive
with `trusted_root`.

fulcio_url.description:
Default Fulcio base URL for `ocx package sign` when `--fulcio-url` is
omitted.

rekor_url.description:
Default Rekor base URL for `ocx package sign` / `verify` when
`--rekor-url` is omitted.

rekor_upload.description:
Fleet-wide default for uploading a **key-mode** signature to the
transparency log, when neither `--rekor-upload` nor `--no-rekor-upload`
is given.

Absent means off. **Key mode only**: keyless signing always uploads, and ignores this
field without a warning. `rekor_url` defaults to the **public** Rekor, where an upload
publishes the artifact's digest and signer to a world-readable log.
